subproblem.title: The cut-off radial operator ω ↦ ζ·Kω: a linear map 𝒟^{q+2}(ℝ^P) → 𝒟^{q+1}(ℝ^P) that equals Kω on ball(0, ρ), with ‖ζ·Kω‖ ≤ (ρ+1)·sup‖ω‖
subproblem.statement:
Let P, q ∈ ℕ and ρ > 0. For a (q+2)-form β on ℝ^P (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q+1+1)) put
 (Kβ)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^{q+1}·ι_x(β(t x)) dt,
where ι_xα := α.curryLeft x, i.e. (ι_xα)(v_1, …, v_{q+1}) = α(x, v_1, …, v_{q+1}).
Assume (H): for every C^∞ (q+2)-form β (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) β: smoothness order ∞, not analytic), the (q+1)-form Kβ is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)).
Then there is an ℝ-linear map Φ : 𝒟^{q+2}(ℝ^P) → 𝒟^{q+1}(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ (q+1+1) →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn univ (q+1)) such that:
(i) (Φω)(x) = (Kω)(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{q+2}(ℝ^P) and every x with ‖x‖ < ρ;
(ii) if b ∈ ℝ and ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ b for every y ∈ ℝ^P (operator norm on covectors), then ‖(Φω)(x)‖ ≤ (ρ+1)·b for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
(H) is the smoothness half of dimred_cs_sos_cfs_radial_homotopy at degree q+1. The selected node discharges it when it assembles its children.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → (∀ β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1 + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) β → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fun x : Euclid P => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ (q + 1) • (β (t • x)).curryLeft x)) → ∃ Φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (q + 1 + 1) →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (q + 1), (∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (q + 1 + 1)) (x : Euclid P), ‖x‖ < ρ → (Φ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1)) x = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ (q + 1) • ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1 + 1)) (t • x)).curryLeft x) ∧ ∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (q + 1 + 1)) (b : ℝ), (∀ y, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1 + 1)) y‖ ≤ b) → ∀ x, ‖(Φ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1)) x‖ ≤ (ρ + 1) * b
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the selected parent proof (the cutoff ζ; the test forms η_ω := ζ·Kω, their linearity in ω, and η_ω = Kω near spt X), together with the a = 0 estimate of its step 3 (‖Kω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε‖x‖ and ‖η_{ω_j}(x)‖ ≤ (ρ+1)ε). The parent takes the smoothness of Kω from radial_homotopy. Here it is the hypothesis (H).

1. Cutoff. Let ζ be the ContDiffBump centred at 0 ∈ ℝ^P with rIn = ρ and rOut = ρ + 1; this is admissible since 0 < ρ < ρ + 1. ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional inner product space, so the ContDiffBump API gives:
 - ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ is C^∞ (contDiff) and has compact support (hasCompactSupport);
 - 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 (nonneg, le_one);
 - ζ(x) = 1 if ‖x‖ ≤ ρ (one_of_mem_closedBall);
 - ζ(x) = 0 if ‖x‖ ≥ ρ + 1 (zero_of_le_dist).

2. The integrands are interval integrable. α ↦ α.curryLeft is a linear isometry Λ^{q+2} → L(ℝ^P, Λ^{q+1}) (curryLeftLI, norm_curryLeft), hence continuous. Let β be a continuous (q+2)-form and x ∈ ℝ^P. Then t ↦ β(t x) is continuous, so t ↦ (β(t x)).curryLeft is continuous. Evaluating this continuously varying continuous linear map at the fixed vector x gives a continuous map t ↦ (β(t x)).curryLeft x. Hence t ↦ t^{q+1}·(β(t x)).curryLeft x is continuous, and in particular interval integrable on [0, 1].

3. K is linear on test forms. Test forms are C^∞, hence continuous. Let ω, ω' ∈ 𝒟^{q+2}(ℝ^P), c ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^P.
 (a) Additivity. (ω + ω')(t x) = ω(t x) + ω'(t x). curryLeft is additive (curryLeft_add), evaluation at x is additive, and t^{q+1}· distributes over sums. Both integrands are interval integrable by step 2, so intervalIntegral.integral_add gives K(ω + ω')(x) = Kω(x) + Kω'(x).
 (b) Homogeneity. (cω)(t x) = c·ω(t x), curryLeft commutes with scalars (curryLeft_smul), and t^{q+1}·(c·v) = c·(t^{q+1}·v) (smul_comm). Pulling the constant c out of the interval integral (intervalIntegral.integral_smul) gives K(cω)(x) = c·Kω(x).

4. The test forms η_ω. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{q+2}(ℝ^P). Since ω is C^∞, Kω is C^∞ by (H). Put η_ω(x) := ζ(x)·Kω(x).
 - η_ω is C^∞, as the product of the C^∞ scalar function ζ and the C^∞ form Kω (ContDiff.smul).
 - Its support lies in the support of ζ, so η_ω has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
 - tsupport η_ω ⊆ ℝ^P trivially.
 Hence η_ω ∈ 𝒟^{q+1}(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ (q+1).

5. The linear map. Define Φω := η_ω. By step 3:
 - η_{ω+ω'}(x) = ζ(x)·(Kω(x) + Kω'(x)) = η_ω(x) + η_{ω'}(x);
 - η_{cω}(x) = ζ(x)·(c·Kω(x)) = c·η_ω(x) (smul_comm).
 Two elements of TestFormOn univ (q+1) with the same underlying form are equal (Subtype.ext). So Φ is ℝ-linear.

6. Property (i). Let ‖x‖ < ρ. Then ‖x‖ ≤ ρ = rIn, so ζ(x) = 1 by step 1, and
 (Φω)(x) = 1·Kω(x) = Kω(x) = ∫_0^1 t^{q+1}·(ω(t x)).curryLeft x dt.

7. Property (ii). Let b ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ b for all y. Then b ≥ ‖ω(0)‖ ≥ 0. Fix x.
 (a) If ‖x‖ ≥ ρ + 1, then ζ(x) = 0, so ‖(Φω)(x)‖ = 0 ≤ (ρ + 1)·b.
 (b) Let ‖x‖ < ρ + 1, and let t ∈ (0, 1]. Then ‖t^{q+1}‖ = t^{q+1} ≤ 1, and
  ‖(ω(t x)).curryLeft x‖ ≤ ‖(ω(t x)).curryLeft‖·‖x‖ = ‖ω(t x)‖·‖x‖ ≤ b‖x‖
 (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm, ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_curryLeft). So the integrand has norm ≤ b‖x‖ on (0, 1] = uIoc 0 1. By intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const,
  ‖Kω(x)‖ ≤ b‖x‖·|1 − 0| = b‖x‖.
 Since 0 ≤ ζ(x) ≤ 1, ‖x‖ < ρ + 1 and b ≥ 0,
  ‖(Φω)(x)‖ = |ζ(x)|·‖Kω(x)‖ ≤ 1·b‖x‖ ≤ (ρ + 1)·b. ∎

(A Lean proof following exactly these steps compiled during decomposition against the frozen contract. It depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Linearity there is checked through hKadd : K(↑ω + ↑ω') = Kω + Kω' and hKsmul : K(c • ↑ω) = c • Kω, stated on the underlying forms.)
proof_key_steps: ζ := ContDiffBump at 0 with radii ρ < ρ+1: C^∞, compactly supported, 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on closedBall(0, ρ), ζ = 0 off ball(0, ρ+1).
The integrands t ↦ t^{q+1}·(ω(t x)).curryLeft x are continuous, so K is additive and homogeneous in ω (curryLeft_add/smul, intervalIntegral.integral_add/integral_smul).
η_ω := ζ·Kω is a test form by (H), ContDiff.smul and HasCompactSupport.smul_right; Φω := η_ω is ℝ-linear (Subtype.ext).
ζ = 1 for ‖x‖ < ρ gives Φω = Kω there. ‖(ω(t x)).curryLeft x‖ ≤ b‖x‖, 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 and ζ = 0 for ‖x‖ ≥ ρ+1 give ‖(Φω)(x)‖ ≤ (ρ+1)b.

audit.reason: All hypotheses, including radial smoothness H and ρ > 0, are explicit and match the type. Continuous integrands justify integral linearity; the bump product is a smooth compactly supported test form. The bound at zero implies b ≥ 0, and the contraction estimate gives exactly (ρ+1)b. The proof supplies the construction without circular reliance.

subproblem.title: Localized radial homotopy formula with a compactly supported primitive: K₁(dγ) = γ − dψ on ball(0, ρ)
subproblem.statement:
Let P, q ∈ ℕ and ρ ∈ ℝ, and write ι_xα := α.curryLeft x. For a (q+1)-form β on ℝ^P and a (q+2)-form α put
 (K₀β)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^q·ι_x(β(t x)) dt,  (K₁α)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^{q+1}·ι_x(α(t x)) dt.
Assume (H): for every C^∞ (q+1)-form β (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) β: smoothness order ∞, not analytic), K₀β is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), and d(K₀β)(x) + K₁(dβ)(x) = β(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P (d = exteriorDerivative).
Then for every test form γ ∈ 𝒟^{q+1}(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ (q+1)) there is a test form ψ ∈ 𝒟^q(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ q) with K₁(dγ)(x) = γ(x) − dψ(x) for every x with ‖x‖ < ρ.
(H) is exactly the statement of dimred_cs_sos_cfs_radial_homotopy at (P, q). The selected node discharges it when it assembles its children.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), (∀ β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) β → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fun x : Euclid P => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ q • (β (t • x)).curryLeft x) ∧ ∀ x : Euclid P, exteriorDerivative (fun y : Euclid P => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ q • (β (t • y)).curryLeft y) x + (∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ (q + 1) • (exteriorDerivative β (t • x)).curryLeft x) = β x) → ∀ γ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (q + 1), ∃ ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) q, ∀ x : Euclid P, ‖x‖ < ρ → (∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ (q + 1) • (exteriorDerivative (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1)) (t • x)).curryLeft x) = (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1)) x - exteriorDerivative (ψ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) q) x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the selected parent proof: the cutoff ψ := ζ·K₀γ, its smoothness and compact support, locality of d, and the homotopy formula. Here it is isolated as a statement about K₁(dγ) alone.

1. Homotopy formula for γ. γ is a test form, so it is C^∞ (first component of its membership in TestFormOn univ (q+1)). Applying (H) with β := γ: K₀γ is C^∞, and d(K₀γ)(x) + K₁(dγ)(x) = γ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.

2. Cutoff. Let ζ be the ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = |ρ| + 1 and rOut = |ρ| + 2, so 0 < rIn < rOut. Then:
 - ζ is C^∞ and has compact support;
 - for every x ∈ ball(0, rIn), ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of x (ContDiffBump.eventuallyEq_one_of_mem_ball).
 The radius |ρ| + 1 is positive even when ρ ≤ 0; in that case the conclusion is vacuous.

3. The primitive ψ. Put ψ(y) := ζ(y)·K₀γ(y).
 - ψ is C^∞, by ContDiff.smul of ζ and the C^∞ form K₀γ from step 1.
 - ψ has compact support, since ζ does (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
 - tsupport ψ ⊆ ℝ^P.
 So ψ ∈ TestFormOn univ q.

4. Locality. Let ‖x‖ < ρ. Then ‖x‖ < |ρ| + 1 = rIn, i.e. x ∈ ball(0, rIn). By step 2, ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of x. There ψ = 1·K₀γ = K₀γ, i.e. ψ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] K₀γ. The exterior derivative at x is built from the Fréchet derivative at x, so it depends only on the germ of the form at x (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq). Hence dψ(x) = d(K₀γ)(x).

5. Conclusion. By step 1, K₁(dγ)(x) = γ(x) − d(K₀γ)(x). By step 4 this equals γ(x) − dψ(x). ∎

(A Lean proof following exactly these steps compiled during decomposition against the frozen contract. It depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.)
proof_key_steps: (H) with β := γ (a C^∞ test form): K₀γ is C^∞ and d(K₀γ) + K₁(dγ) = γ everywhere.
ψ := ζ·K₀γ is a test q-form, where ζ is a bump equal to 1 near every point of ball(0, |ρ|+1).
For ‖x‖ < ρ, ψ = K₀γ near x, so dψ(x) = d(K₀γ)(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq), whence K₁(dγ)(x) = γ(x) − dψ(x).

audit.reason: H matches the existing radial-homotopy contract at (P,q). The bump with inner radius |ρ|+1 works for every real ρ. Germ equality identifies the exterior derivatives, and rearranging H yields the exact conclusion. The supplied proof is complete; an independent formalization compiled with only standard axioms.

subproblem.title: Vanishing on the carrier and the C⁰ bound |X(γ)| ≤ μ_R(ℝ^P)·sup‖γ‖ for a current represented by an integer multiplicity triple
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) representing X (R.Represents X). That is, X(γ) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(γ(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Hⁿ = μHE[n].
Then:
(a) if γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and γ(x) = 0 for every x ∈ M = R.carrier, then X(γ) = 0;
(b) if μ_R(ℝ^P) := R.measure univ = ∫_M θ dHⁿ is finite, then |X(γ)| ≤ μ_R(ℝ^P)·b for every γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and b ∈ ℝ with ‖γ(x)‖ ≤ b for all x ∈ ℝ^P. Here ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n, and μ_R(ℝ^P) is read as the real number (R.measure univ).toReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents X → (∀ γ : TestFormOn U n, (∀ x ∈ R.carrier, (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x = 0) → X γ = 0) ∧ (R.measure univ ≠ ∞ → ∀ (γ : TestFormOn U n) (b : ℝ), (∀ x, ‖(γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x‖ ≤ b) → |X γ| ≤ (R.measure univ).toReal * b)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 of the selected parent proof ((0a) vanishing and (0b) C⁰ bound), stated for an arbitrary domain U and degree n, and with the vanishing hypothesis required only on the carrier M. The selected node applies it with U = ℝ^P, n = q + 1, and M ⊆ spt X.

Notation. M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ (measurable), ξ := R.orient, Hⁿ := μHE[n], and μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M. By R.Represents X and the definition of IMRep.action, for every γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U):
 (∗) X(γ) = ∫_M (θ(x) : ℝ)·ξ(x)(γ(x)) dHⁿ(x).

1. Part (a). Let γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with γ(x) = 0 for every x ∈ M. For x ∈ M, ξ(x) is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors, so ξ(x)(γ(x)) = ξ(x)(0) = 0 (map_zero). The integrand of (∗) is therefore θ(x)·0 = 0 at every point of M. A set integral whose integrand vanishes at every point of the set is 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero), so X(γ) = 0.

2. Part (b): orientation bound. By the field R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. That is, there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P with ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or with ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α. For such x and every n-covector α,
 |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖,
by ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm and ‖τ_i‖ = 1 (orthonormality). For n = 0 the product is empty and equals 1. Hence, for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every α.

3. Mass identity. R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, so R.measure univ = ∫⁻_M θ dHⁿ (withDensity_apply with the measurable set univ, then Measure.restrict_univ).

4. Integrability of θ. Assume R.measure univ ≠ ∞. The function x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞) is measurable: θ is measurable, and every function on ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat). By step 3 its μ-lintegral is R.measure univ < ∞. Hence x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞).toReal = (θ(x) : ℝ) is μ-integrable (integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top). Since every θ(x) < ∞, integral_toReal gives
 ∫ (θ(x) : ℝ) dμ = (∫⁻ θ dμ).toReal = (R.measure univ).toReal.

5. Estimate. Let γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and b ∈ ℝ with ‖γ(x)‖ ≤ b for all x. By step 2 and θ(x) ≥ 0, for μ-a.e. x:
 |θ(x)·ξ(x)(γ(x))| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(γ(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖γ(x)‖ ≤ θ(x)·b.
The function x ↦ θ(x)·b is μ-integrable (step 4, times the constant b). Applying norm_integral_le_of_norm_le to (∗):
 |X(γ)| ≤ ∫ θ(x)·b dμ = (∫ θ dμ)·b = (R.measure univ).toReal·b,
by integral_mul_const and step 4. ∎
